topicName: Transport of Materials in the Human Body
description: An introduction to the human circulatory system, covering the heart and its chambers, the blood vessels, the components of blood, and how valves and blood groups keep materials moving safely around the body.

mcq.questionText: The organ that pumps blood around the human body is the:
mcq.explanation: The heart is a muscular pump that keeps blood circulating. Exam Tip: The heart is cardiac muscle and never tires.

mcq.questionText: The human heart is divided into how many chambers?
mcq.explanation: Two atria (upper) and two ventricles (lower) make four chambers. Exam Tip: Four chambers keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate.

mcq.questionText: The blood vessels that carry blood AWAY from the heart are called:
mcq.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Exam Tip: Arteries = Away (both start with A); veins carry blood back.

mcq.questionText: The blood vessels that carry blood BACK to the heart are called:
mcq.explanation: Veins carry blood back towards the heart. Exam Tip: Veins have valves to stop backflow because the blood is at low pressure.

mcq.questionText: The tiny, thin-walled blood vessels where exchange of materials between blood and cells takes place are the:
mcq.explanation: Capillaries have walls one cell thick, allowing exchange. Exam Tip: Capillaries connect arteries to veins and are the exchange sites.

mcq.questionText: The component of blood that transports oxygen is the:
mcq.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen. Exam Tip: Red is for oxygen, white is for defence, and platelets are for clotting.

mcq.questionText: The red pigment in red blood cells that combines with oxygen is called:
mcq.explanation: Haemoglobin, which contains iron, carries oxygen. Exam Tip: Haemoglobin plus oxygen forms oxyhaemoglobin.

mcq.questionText: The main function of white blood cells is to:
mcq.explanation: White blood cells fight germs and defend the body. Exam Tip: White blood cells engulf germs and make antibodies.

mcq.questionText: The blood cells (fragments) responsible for clotting of blood are the:
mcq.explanation: Platelets trigger the clotting process. Exam Tip: Platelets cause clotting, which stops bleeding.

mcq.questionText: The liquid part of blood in which cells are suspended is called:
mcq.explanation: The pale-yellow liquid part of blood is plasma. Exam Tip: Plasma transports dissolved food, wastes, hormones and carbon dioxide.

mcq.questionText: The largest artery in the body, which carries oxygenated blood from the heart, is the:
mcq.explanation: Blood leaves the left ventricle through the aorta. Exam Tip: The aorta is the biggest artery and the vena cava is the biggest vein.

mcq.questionText: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body?
mcq.explanation: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the body. Exam Tip: The left ventricle has the thickest wall.

mcq.questionText: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle?

options.text: It pumps blood only to the lungs
It pumps blood at high pressure to the whole body

mcq.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood all around the body at high pressure, while the right only pumps to the lungs. Exam Tip: More distance and higher pressure means thicker muscle.

mcq.questionText: The structures that prevent the backflow of blood in the heart and veins are the:
mcq.explanation: Valves open one way and close to stop backflow. Exam Tip: Valves keep blood moving forward only.

mcq.questionText: A person with blood group O is called a "universal donor" because:

options.text: They can receive blood from anyone
Their blood can be given to people of all ABO blood groups

mcq.explanation: Group O red cells have no A or B antigens, so they can be given to A, B, AB and O. Exam Tip: O is the universal DONOR and AB is the universal RECIPIENT.

fib.questionText: The muscular organ that pumps blood around the body is the ____.
fib.explanation: The heart is the muscular pump that keeps blood circulating. Exam Tip: The heart is cardiac muscle that never tires.

fib.questionText: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are called ____.
fib.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart and have thick, elastic walls. Exam Tip: Arteries = Away; thick, elastic walls.

fib.questionText: The red pigment in red blood cells that carries oxygen is ____.
fib.explanation: Haemoglobin contains iron and binds oxygen for transport. Exam Tip: Haemoglobin contains iron and binds oxygen.

fib.questionText: The tiny blood vessels where exchange of substances with tissues occurs are the ____.
fib.explanation: Capillaries have walls one cell thick, so substances exchange easily. Exam Tip: Capillary walls are one cell thick.

fib.questionText: The liquid part of blood is called ____.
fib.explanation: Plasma is the pale-yellow liquid in which blood cells are suspended. Exam Tip: Plasma carries dissolved food, hormones, wastes and carbon dioxide.

fib.questionText: The blood cells that defend the body against disease are the ____ blood cells.
fib.explanation: White blood cells engulf germs and produce antibodies to defend the body. Exam Tip: White blood cells engulf germs and produce antibodies.

fib.questionText: The chamber of the heart with the thickest muscular wall is the left ____.
fib.explanation: The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood around the whole body. Exam Tip: The left ventricle pumps blood around the whole body.

fib.questionText: Blood cells that help in the clotting of blood are called ____.
fib.explanation: Platelets seal wounds by forming clots that stop bleeding. Exam Tip: Platelets seal wounds by forming clots.

fib.questionText: The largest vein that returns deoxygenated blood to the heart is the ____.
fib.explanation: The vena cava is the largest vein and returns deoxygenated blood to the heart. Exam Tip: The vena cava is the largest vein and the aorta is the largest artery.

fib.questionText: Structures in the veins and heart that prevent backflow of blood are called ____.
fib.explanation: Valves open one way only, so blood cannot flow backwards. Exam Tip: Valves keep blood moving forward only.

tf.questionText: The human heart has four chambers.
tf.explanation: The heart has two atria and two ventricles, making four chambers. Exam Tip: Four chambers keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood apart.

tf.questionText: Arteries carry blood back to the heart.
tf.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back. Exam Tip: Arteries = Away; veins = back. This statement swaps them.

tf.questionText: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which carries oxygen.
tf.explanation: Red blood cells are packed with haemoglobin that binds and transports oxygen. Exam Tip: Red blood cells carry out oxygen transport.

tf.questionText: White blood cells carry oxygen around the body.
tf.explanation: Red blood cells carry oxygen; white blood cells defend the body against disease. Exam Tip: Red is for oxygen, white is for defence.

tf.questionText: Capillaries are the vessels where exchange of gases and nutrients takes place.
tf.explanation: Capillary walls are one cell thick, allowing efficient exchange with tissues. Exam Tip: Capillary walls one cell thick means efficient exchange.

tf.questionText: The left ventricle has a thicker wall than the right ventricle.
tf.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood at high pressure to the whole body, so its wall is thicker. Exam Tip: A thicker wall means higher pressure and pumping further, to the whole body.

tf.questionText: Platelets are responsible for carrying oxygen in the blood.
tf.explanation: Platelets cause clotting; red blood cells carry oxygen. Exam Tip: Platelets are for clotting; red cells are for oxygen.

tf.questionText: Valves in the heart and veins prevent the backflow of blood.
tf.explanation: Valves open one way and close to keep blood flowing in a single direction. Exam Tip: Valves ensure one-way blood flow.

tf.questionText: Plasma is the liquid part of blood that transports dissolved substances.
tf.explanation: Plasma is the liquid medium that carries dissolved food, wastes, hormones and carbon dioxide. Exam Tip: Plasma is the transport medium for dissolved materials.

tf.questionText: A person with blood group AB is called the universal donor.
tf.explanation: Group O is the universal donor; group AB is the universal recipient. Exam Tip: O is the universal donor and AB is the universal recipient. This statement swaps them.

summary.correctAnswer: The muscular organ that pumps blood around the body through the circulatory system.
summary.explanation: It is made of cardiac muscle that contracts continuously without tiring. Exam Tip: The heart is a double pump that keeps blood circulating.

summary.correctAnswer: The two atria (upper chambers) that receive blood and the two ventricles (lower chambers) that pump blood out.
summary.explanation: The four chambers keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate. Exam Tip: Atria receive blood; ventricles pump it out.

summary.correctAnswer: Blood vessels with thick, elastic walls that carry blood away from the heart at high pressure.
summary.explanation: The largest artery is the aorta, and arteries have no valves except at the heart. Exam Tip: Arteries = Away from the heart.

summary.correctAnswer: Blood vessels with thinner walls and valves that carry blood back to the heart at low pressure.
summary.explanation: Valves in veins prevent the low-pressure blood from flowing backwards. Exam Tip: Veins return blood to the heart and contain valves.

summary.correctAnswer: The smallest blood vessels, with walls one cell thick, where exchange of materials between blood and cells occurs.
summary.explanation: They connect arteries to veins and are the sites of gas and nutrient exchange. Exam Tip: Capillary walls one cell thick allow rapid exchange.

summary.correctAnswer: Red blood cells are cells containing haemoglobin, the iron-rich red pigment that binds and transports oxygen.
summary.explanation: Haemoglobin combines with oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin. Exam Tip: Red cells plus haemoglobin equal oxygen transport.

summary.correctAnswer: Blood cells that defend the body against disease by engulfing germs and producing antibodies.
summary.explanation: They are part of the body's immune defence system. Exam Tip: White blood cells fight infection and make antibodies.

summary.correctAnswer: Small cell fragments in the blood that trigger clotting to stop bleeding.
summary.explanation: They form clots that seal wounds and prevent blood loss. Exam Tip: Platelets lead to clotting.

summary.correctAnswer: The pale-yellow liquid part of blood in which cells are suspended and dissolved substances are carried.
summary.explanation: It transports dissolved food, wastes, hormones and carbon dioxide. Exam Tip: Plasma is the transport medium for dissolved materials.

summary.correctAnswer: Valves are structures in the heart and veins that prevent backflow, and blood groups (A, B, AB, O) classify blood by its antigens.
summary.explanation: Valves ensure one-way flow, while group O is the universal donor and AB the universal recipient. Exam Tip: Valves keep blood one-way; O donates to all, AB receives from all.

hoq.questionText: Trace the correct path of a drop of blood from the body, through the right side of the heart, to the lungs.

options.text: Body -> vena cava -> right atrium -> right ventricle -> pulmonary artery -> lungs
Body -> pulmonary vein -> left atrium -> lungs

hoq.explanation: Deoxygenated blood enters via the vena cava into the right atrium, then the right ventricle, then the pulmonary artery to the lungs. Exam Tip: The RIGHT side handles DEOXYGENATED blood to the lungs, and the pulmonary ARTERY is the exception carrying deoxygenated blood.

hoq.questionText: Vessel X has a thick elastic wall, no valves, high pressure and flow away from the heart. Vessel Y has a thin wall, valves present, low pressure and flow towards the heart. Identify X and Y and explain the valves in Y.

options.text: X = vein, Y = artery; valves store blood
X = artery, Y = vein; valves in the vein prevent backflow of low-pressure blood

hoq.explanation: X is thick, high pressure and carries blood away, so it is an artery, while Y is thin with valves, low pressure and carries blood towards the heart, so it is a vein; low-pressure blood in veins needs valves to stop backflow. Exam Tip: thick + elastic + high pressure + away = artery; thin + valves + low pressure + towards = vein.

hoq.questionText: A patient is very tired, short of breath and pale, with low haemoglobin. The doctor advises iron-rich foods such as green vegetables and liver. Explain the link.

options.text: Low haemoglobin means less oxygen is carried, causing tiredness (anaemia); iron is needed to make haemoglobin, so iron-rich foods help
Iron has no role in blood
The patient has too many red blood cells

hoq.explanation: Haemoglobin carries oxygen, so low haemoglobin means less oxygen reaches the tissues (anaemia), and because iron is part of haemoglobin, iron-rich foods let the body make more. Exam Tip: Follow the chain iron -> haemoglobin -> oxygen transport; treatment restores the missing item, which is iron.
